sources.field_scope: Great Lakes fishing guide page. A guide license is issued to a person paid to guide, direct, or assist someone fishing on the Great Lakes and tributaries by any means other than sport trolling for salmon and trout. It is also required for species other than trout and salmon on outlying waters, and for pre-placed ice-fishing structures. Renting a boat or gear for independent use, without further guiding, is not guiding. A U.S. Coast Guard license is still required to guide passengers from a vessel on those waters. Licenses are bought in Go Wild or at a sales location and run January 1 through December 31. A business that hires guides may itself hold a guide license and report for its staff for a full calendar year. Electronic trip reports use Survey123 within 24 hours where reporting is required. The page's 2027-and-onward reporting locations are Green Bay for all species, Lake Michigan smallmouth bass in Door County waters only, and Lake Superior for all species. Sheboygan is not one of those locations. No licensee roster is on the page. Staff names were not stored.
sources.bulk: No roster download. Forms and grid maps are separate files.
sources.request_process: Reporting is a licensee duty in Survey123. It is not a public file and not a reuse grant.
sources.rights_basis: DNR website content. Acceptable use limits the material to noncommercial use of the general public, applies fair use, and requires permission from the page contact for other copying.

sources.field_scope: Charter sport-trolling page. An outlying-water sport-trolling license is required to guide salmon or trout by sport trolling on Lake Superior, Lake Michigan, and Green Bay, including tributaries up to the first fish impasse. The licensee is the person. Boats used by the licensee must meet U.S. Coast Guard and Wisconsin boat requirements. The page says licenses may be issued only to persons over 18. Returning captains buy the license in Go Wild. It is valid January 1 through December 31. New captains mail Form 9400-245. Electronic reporting has been required since May 1, 2023, including months with no trips after the license is purchased. Within 30 minutes of returning, the report includes the captain's customer ID, name, boat information, trip location, angler count, hours, and total harvest. Species harvest is due by 11:59 p.m. the same day. The month is transmitted by the 10th. No public roster of licensees or boats is on the page. An organizational mailbox is named and was not stored or used.
sources.bulk: Linked forms and grid maps are separate files. No licensee download.
sources.request_process: The mailbox is for charter reporting accounts. It was not used. It is not a reuse grant.
sources.rights_basis: DNR website content under the acceptable-use policy.

sources.field_scope: Commercial licenses index. Guide, bait, fur, and taxidermy licenses are bought in Go Wild. The page says there is no longer a paper application for those, and a Department of Revenue check happens at purchase. A nonresident guide license covers fishing only. The sport-trolling row says the license is required to guide sport trolling for trout or salmon on the outlying waters and may be issued to a person over the age of 17. It links Form 9400-245. It does not list holders, ports, or boats.
sources.request_process: A toll-free customer-service number is printed for commercial-license questions. It was not used.

sources.field_scope: Acceptable use policy for dnr.wi.gov. The page says the material is for the noncommercial use of the general public and that fair-use guidelines apply. It says the department remains the sole owner of specifically copyrighted information it created and posted. Photographs and graphics are property of the department or of an agency that holds a license to display them. Use outside fair use requires permission from the person listed as responsible for the page, or from the department if no page contact can be identified. If permission to reproduce or redistribute is granted, the credit must read: Reproduced with permission from the Department of Natural Resources. Links to dnr.wi.gov are welcome. The department will not make reciprocal link agreements. A link is not an endorsement. No date is printed on the policy.
sources.attribution: The required credit applies only after permission to reproduce or redistribute is granted. No permission was requested.
sources.request_process: Ask the listed page contact, or the department if the page contact cannot be identified. No request was sent.
sources.rights_basis: This is the policy for the DNR pages and PDFs opened here. It does not grant a commercial directory license. Terms for a later public-records file are not stated on this page.

sources.field_scope: Public records request page. Email is described as the preferred way to submit a request. A form, 9500-096, is optional. Requests after 5 p.m. start the next business day. Copying is $0.0113 per black-and-white side. Scanning is waived. Location is $25 an hour when the cost is $50 or more, and the department may pre-bill under Wis. Stat. 19.35(3)(f). Review for redaction is not charged. Electronic copies of records that already exist electronically are not charged per page. Questions are not records requests. No request was sent. The page does not say whether a sport-trolling licensee list or trip-report boat names would be released.
sources.bulk: No sport-trolling download is linked from this page.
sources.request_process: The page names an organizational mailbox and a coordinator phone number. Neither was used, and neither was copied into this note. A request would be for records, not a standing commercial-reuse grant.
sources.rights_basis: The page describes how to ask for records and what copying costs. It does not state reuse terms for a file that has not been released. Website text remains under the acceptable-use policy.

sources.field_scope: Compiled statutes displayed from the 29.512 address. Section 29.512 requires a guide license before a person is employed for compensation to guide, direct, or assist another person in hunting, fishing, or trapping. Hunting and trapping guide licenses are resident-only. No guide license may be issued under age 18. Section 29.514, on the same retrieved compilation, requires a sport-trolling license before a person is employed for compensation to guide sport trolling for trout or salmon on the outlying waters. No sport-trolling license may be issued under age 18. The application must include the applicant's name and address, the home port from which the applicant will operate, the applicant's valid U.S. Coast Guard operator's license number, and other information the department requires. The licensee and everyone aboard must comply with this chapter. Boats used by the licensee must meet Coast Guard and state boat requirements. Subsection (2) requires monthly records of fish taken, due by the 10th day of the next month. The statute does not say the boat holds the license. Legislature site reuse terms were not on this display.
sources.rights_basis: The sections create person licenses and a reporting duty. They do not publish a roster and do not grant commercial reuse of licensee or boat records.

sources.field_scope: Fee schedule subsection 29.563(5), read from the legislature's displayed compilation and from the chapter PDF text, which agreed. Resident guide $39.25. Resident sport trolling $100. Nonresident guide $99.25. Nonresident Lake Michigan and Green Bay sport trolling $400. Nonresident Lake Superior sport trolling $400. A separate issuing-fee subsection was not reconciled to the 25-cent amounts printed on the application form. Proposal text that would raise these fees was visible in search and was not treated as law. The compiled amounts above are the ones read as current.
sources.rights_basis: A fee statute is not a directory license.

sources.publisher: Wisconsin Legislative Reference Bureau, administrative code display
sources.field_scope: NR 20.60, monthly sport-trolling reports, and the start of NR 20.65, guide reports, on the same display. NR 20.60 requires the electronic system except during an outage. For each trip the licensee records name, license number, date, documented boat name or 8-digit state registration number, locations fished, anglers, hours, and harvest, within half an hour of returning to the dock or shore. Species detail is due by 11:59 p.m. that day. The month is submitted by the 10th. A month with no trips still needs a no-trip report. Paper copies are kept five years. The report must be shown to a department representative on request. History on the section shows the electronic-reporting rewrite effective May 1, 2023. NR 20.65 defines a fishing guide as a person licensed under 29.512 and lets an employing guide licensee report for its guides for the license year. The guide report fields in the portion read include guide identity, date, location, anglers, hours, and fish. A boat-name field was not in that guide-report list. Neither section publishes the reports.
sources.bulk: The reports are entered in a department system. No public extract is linked from the rule text.
sources.request_process: Exhibition to a department representative is an enforcement duty, not a public download.
sources.rights_basis: The rule tells licensees what to file. It does not release the file or license commercial reuse. The boat name or registration number exists in the sport-trolling report and is not posted.

sources.field_scope: Blank Form 9400-245, revision R 1/22, Outlying Water Sport Trolling License Application. PDFKit reported one page. It says use is required for an application under s. 29.514. It says collected information may be used for surveys, eligibility, law enforcement, and other secondary purposes, and that the department may provide the information to requesters under the public records law, ss. 19.31 to 19.39. Printed fees are $100.25 resident and $400.25 nonresident. The license expires December 31. Payment is not sent with the form. Fields in the extracted text are name, email, address, phone, date of birth, sex, DNR customer ID, residency, and fishing location checkboxes for Lake Michigan, Lake Superior, and Green Bay. The certification says the applicant's U.S. Coast Guard operator's license number is current and that the applicant will not use a boat that fails Coast Guard or Wisconsin boat requirements. A labeled home-port blank and a labeled boat-name blank were not in the extracted text. The statute still requires the home port and the Coast Guard number on the application. Mail goes to the Sturgeon Bay Service Center. This is a blank form, not a roster.
sources.bulk: One blank PDF. No issued-license file.
sources.request_process: Mail the application to the service center named on the form. That path was not used. The public-records sentence is about information the department holds, not a license to copy a directory.
sources.rights_basis: The PDF is DNR website content. Its public-records sentence does not identify which fields would be released or authorize commercial reuse.

sources.field_scope: Guide and Sport Trolling Informational Document, revised 03/2022. Two pages. It says it is an interpreted summary and points readers to the statutes and administrative code. It repeats the guide-versus-sport-trolling split. It prints new-guide costs of $40 resident and $100 nonresident, and sport-trolling costs of $100.25 resident and $400.25 nonresident, with a minimum age of 18. It says a valid operator's license number must be provided on the sport-trolling application, and that a Coast Guard operator's license is required to carry passengers for hire on federally navigable waters. It defines outlying waters by citing s. 29.001(63) as Lake Superior, Lake Michigan, Green Bay, Sturgeon Bay, Sawyer's Harbor, and the Fox River from its mouth to the dam at De Pere. Section 29.001 was not opened separately. The sheet says the licensee is responsible for the number of fish taken aboard the boat. It is not a roster. The March 2022 fee lines do not match the compiled statute amounts read the same day.
sources.rights_basis: DNR website PDF. Dated March 2022. It is not the fee statute.

sources.field_scope: Lake Michigan and Green Bay sportfishing effort and harvest tables. PDFKit reported 14 pages. Page 1 says the tables show estimated angler effort and harvest of trout and salmon. Table 1 is total fishing effort in angler hours by angler group from 2011 through 2025. The 2025 charter column is 256,540 angler hours. The 2025 total across ramp, moored, charter, pier, shore, and stream is 2,307,077. Table 2 is effort by county for 2021 through 2025, all angler groups together. Sheboygan is 175,574, 213,660, 153,181, 197,849, and 162,117. Later tables count fish harvested by fishery type, including a charter column. Those cells were not copied forward as boat counts. No hull, captain, or trip-count roster is in the pages read. No publication date is printed on page 1.
sources.bulk: One PDF of estimates. No microdata and no stated bulk license.
sources.rights_basis: DNR website PDF. Estimated hours and harvest are not a license to rebuild a charter directory and are not a count of Sheboygan departures.

next_questions: Will the department release a current list of sport-trolling licensees, home ports, or the boat-name field required by NR 20.60?
